content.gout_and_urate_lowering: Allopurinol was associated with a lower rate of all-cause and cardiovascular death compared with febuxostat in a large trial enrolling patients with gout and CV disease; allopurinol is recommended as first-choice urate-lowering drug in HF patients without contraindication. There is no evidence that uric acid-lowering treatment improves LV function, symptoms or outcomes in HF.
content.acute_gout_attack_treatment: NSAIDs can worsen renal function and precipitate acute HF decompensation. Colchicine is preferred as it is associated with fewer side effects but should be used with caution in severe renal dysfunction and is contraindicated in patients on dialysis.
content.arthritis_and_rheumatoid_arthritis: Arthritis is a common comorbidity and a common cause of NSAID use. Rheumatoid arthritis is associated with a two- to three-fold increased risk of HF independent of ischemic heart disease, suggesting a direct role in HF pathophysiology. Safety of disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs in HF is not established; high doses of anti–tumor necrosis factor agents were associated with worsening HF in initial trials and should be used with caution.
content.13.11_erectile_dysfunction: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is common in HF patients due to CV risk factors, comorbidities and treatments. Prevalence in general population ~50% in men aged ≥60; in cardiac patients ED can be present in up to 81%. Assessment should include presence and contributing factors. Numerous CV drugs (particularly diuretics and beta-blockers) have been implicated. Phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitors are generally safe and effective in patients with compensated HF. PDE5 inhibitors must not be used in patients receiving nitrates; nitrates should not be administered within 24 hours of sildenafil or vardenafil, or within 48 hours of tadalafil.
content.13.12_depression: Depression affects ~20% of HF patients and is severe in about half; occurrence higher in women and associated with worse clinical status and poor prognosis. Screening with validated questionnaires is recommended when depression is suspected (Beck Depression Inventory, Cardiac Depression Scale, and others). No consensus on best therapy: psychosocial interventions may improve symptoms but do not affect prognosis. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors may improve depressive symptoms, but trials specifically in HF patients have not demonstrated significant benefit over placebo on symptoms or prognosis.
